children: Shares of HDFC Life, SBI Life Insurance Company and other insurance firms rose up to 5 percent on Thursday amid expectations of lower commission payments to insurance distributors.

The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) is expected to issue a consultation paper soon on insurance commissions and distribution, which is likely to provide direction on the issue, CNBC-TV18 reported, citing sources.
The proposed paper is unlikely to specify limits on commissions or expenses of management, the report said.

According to CNBC-TV18 report, banks are likely to face a significant reduction in commissions, while individual agents may see the smallest reduction. Group life insurance products could face a larger cut, it said.
Shares of life insurance companies gained as investors expect the proposed changes to lower the commissions paid by insurers to distributors if the new norms are implemented.
HDFC Life shares settled more than 5 percent higher at Rs 557 per share on the NSE. The stock was the top gainer on the Nifty 50 during the session.
SBI Life Insurance Company followed, rising more than 4 percent to Rs 1,766.90 on the NSE. It was the third-biggest gainer on the benchmark Nifty.
Max Financial Services rose 4.5 percent, ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company gained 3.2 percent, while The New India Assurance Company rose 7 percent.

Shares of PB Fintech, which operates the insurance marketplace Policybazaar, traded nearly 3 percent lower. The stock declined amid concerns over the potential impact of changes in insurance commission and distribution rules.
